description: The UCSB Climate Hazards Center publishes CHIRPS version two, a gridded rainfall series blending satellite infrared estimates with station observations. Its own page links public NetCDF and GeoTIFF data directories and states that the data are in the public domain. Coverage spans land from 50 degrees south to 50 degrees north, from 1981 toward the present at 0.05-degree resolution. Daily, pentad and monthly products can supply rainfall and drought forcing for water-supply, crop and flood exposure simulations. A caveat is that satellite estimates and sparse gauges can miss local extremes, especially in complex terrain. Preliminary and final products differ because later station reports are incorporated. The provider now also offers CHIRPS version three and says version-two production will end after December 2026, so a modeller should record which version was used. I read the provider page and directory listing without downloading grids or checking station-level errors. No directly related catalogue record was identified.
